scope: Equation-level and mechanism-level prior-art audit of PM/RUT gravitational memory; not exhaustive, not a patent opinion, not a certificate of novelty.
source_policy: Exact mappings use inspected primary equations. Abstract-only records support only abstract-level comparisons. One author review is retained as an explicitly labeled earlier pointer; DLMF is an official reference. Unretrieved leads are separate.

followup_leads.title: On the formulation of rheological equations of state
followup_leads.status: Primary full text not retrieved; bibliographic lead only. AP2024 is the inspected primary source for transported constitutive memory.

followup_leads.title: On the gravitational stability of a disk of stars
followup_leads.status: ADS primary PDF timed out. Follow-up foundational comparison; H1970 and CS2008 support the limited stability context used here.

followup_leads.title: Phase transitions in the Gaussian core system
followup_leads.status: Primary article not retrieved. Do not assert identity with the Gaussian core model: RUT's eliminated interaction is attractive, and the physical sign matters.

sources.title: Modified Newtonian Dynamics in the Milky Way
sources.locator: Equations 1 and 5 and text before/after equation 5
sources.established_overlap: Equation 5 is algebraically identical to Completion I mu_PM; the surrounding text attributes the function to Bekenstein's toy construction.
sources.limit_of_comparison: The source states spherical and acceleration-regime qualifications; equality of this function does not establish equality of complete relativistic or disk theories.

sources.title: Relativistic gravitation theory for the MOND paradigm
sources.established_overlap: Tensor-vector-scalar relativistic construction underlying the attribution made in FB2005.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Exact interpolation identification in this audit is verified in FB2005, not by a new full derivation of TeVeS.

sources.title: Does the missing mass problem signal the breakdown of Newtonian gravity?
sources.locator: Printed pages 7-8, especially section II equations 2b, 3 and 5; page images inspected
sources.established_overlap: Nonlinear-Poisson action, field equation and constitutive derivative relation already exist in AQUAL.
sources.limit_of_comparison: An algebraic acceleration rule and the nonlinear field equation agree only with appropriate symmetry or curl-term conditions.

sources.title: Refining MOND Interpolating Function and TeVeS Lagrangian
sources.established_overlap: Interpolation functions and underlying free-function choices were already explicit subjects of MOND/TeVeS model development.
sources.limit_of_comparison: No claim here that all such functions or theories are equivalent to RUT.

sources.title: Quasi-linear formulation of MOND
sources.established_overlap: QUMOND gives a separate shared-potential realization of MOND phenomenology.
sources.limit_of_comparison: A shared spherical acceleration law is not sufficient to identify QUMOND with AQUAL or our separate nonlinear auxiliary field.

sources.title: Path-memory induced quantization of classical orbits
sources.authors: Emmanuel Fort; Antonin Eddi; Arezki Boudaoud; Julien Moukhtar; Yves Couder
sources.locator: Abstract; original 2010 paper pointer; PMC full-text retrieval challenged in this audit
sources.established_overlap: Persistent waves written along droplet paths change radial orbital forces and permitted classical orbits.
sources.limit_of_comparison: An externally driven bath and imposed rotation are not a self-powered gravitational field. The journal paper is from 2010, although the arXiv posting is 2013.

sources.title: A trajectory equation for walking droplets: hydrodynamic pilot-wave theory
sources.authors: Anand U. Oza; Rodolfo R. Rosales; John W. M. Bush
sources.established_overlap: Continuous path-history trajectory equations for a droplet coupled to its waves.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Its driven hydrodynamic kernel and drag differ from RUT's attractive Gaussian and central gravitational potential.

sources.title: Orbiting pairs of walking droplets: Dynamics and stability
sources.authors: Anand U. Oza; Emmanuel Siéfert; Daniel M. Harris; Jan Moláček; John W. M. Bush
sources.established_overlap: Orbital stability depends on droplet-wave coupling, including impact-phase adaptation to local wave height.
sources.limit_of_comparison: This is a concrete feedback precedent, not an exact match to the two-stage linear maturation rule.

sources.title: Collective vibrations of a hydrodynamic active lattice
sources.authors: Stuart J. Thomson; Matthew Durey; Rodolfo R. Rosales
sources.locator: Equations 1-2, characteristic equation 14 and geometric versus oscillatory-instability discussion
sources.established_overlap: Particles write a relaxing shared field and respond to its gradient; collective analysis distinguishes geometric instability from memory-dependent instability.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Their driven, viscously damped annular lattice and oscillatory kernel are not the full unconstrained radial RUT model.

sources.title: Collective vibrations of confined levitating droplets
sources.authors: Stuart J. Thomson; Matthew M. P. Couchman; John W. M. Bush
sources.established_overlap: Experimental collective dynamics of wave-mediated droplets confined on an annulus.
sources.limit_of_comparison: External bath forcing and confinement must be retained when comparing with orbital populations.

sources.title: Discrete and periodic complex Ginzburg-Landau equation for a hydrodynamic active lattice
sources.authors: Stuart J. Thomson; Matthew Durey; Rodolfo R. Rosales
sources.established_overlap: Weakly nonlinear amplitude equations connect memory-mediated lattice instability to collective nonlinear states.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Preprint title is A discrete complex Ginzburg-Landau equation for a hydrodynamic active lattice; a shared amplitude-equation method is not identical nonlinear dynamics.

sources.title: Emergent Active Clusters through Wave-Mediated Interactions
sources.locator: Abstract; Results, Emergence of Active Clusters; Wave-mediated collective motion; displayed trajectory-history model
sources.established_overlap: Reports persistent stationary, rotating and translating clusters of droplets that are unstable in isolation, sustained by a shared wavefield.
sources.limit_of_comparison: The isolated instability is bounce desynchronization/coalescence; the model uses a driven bath, oscillatory wave kernel, drag and short-range repulsion. It is not the RUT cold-ring instability.

sources.title: A stochastic Keller-Segel model of chemotaxis
sources.established_overlap: Inertial particles emit a produced/decaying field, respond to its gradient and admit kinetic and continuum descriptions with history dependence.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Diffusion, friction, stochastic forcing, source smearing and confinement differ. Setting those terms to particular limits is an adaptation, not proof of identity of the published physical systems.

sources.title: Kinetic and hydrodynamic models of chemotactic aggregation
sources.established_overlap: Kinetic, inertial and hydrodynamic descriptions of chemotactic aggregation and their relationship to self-gravitating dynamics.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Not an equation-level equivalence to the warm rotating RUT annulus.

sources.title: Jeans type analysis of chemotactic collapse
sources.established_overlap: Pressure/sound-speed thresholds and growth/damping rates for field-mediated aggregation, with inertial and frictional effects.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Temperature suppressing attractive collapse is not a new general principle; our rotating kinetic memory response still needs its own derivation.

sources.title: Dynamics of a microorganism moving by chemotaxis in its own secretion
sources.authors: Ankush Sengupta; Sven van Teeffelen; Hartmut Löwen
sources.established_overlap: Self-interaction with an emitted chemical produces history-dependent arrest and transport regimes.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Diffusing chemical and microorganism transport differ from an inertial orbiting gravitational source.

sources.title: Effective Dynamics of Microorganisms That Interact with Their Own Trail
sources.authors: W. Till Kranz; Anatolij Gelimson; Kun Zhao; Gerard C. L. Wong; Ramin Golestanian
sources.established_overlap: Finite-width persistent trails generate effective history-dependent self-interactions.
sources.limit_of_comparison: The response is primarily an active swimmer's orientation/transport, not RUT's conservative-gradient acceleration plus field dynamics.

sources.title: Clustering and Pattern Formation in Chemorepulsive Active Colloids
sources.authors: Benno Liebchen; Davide Marenduzzo; Ignacio Pagonabarraga; Michael E. Cates
sources.established_overlap: Chemical response dynamics and anisotropy can generate clustering and pattern-forming instabilities even with repulsive chemotaxis.
sources.limit_of_comparison: A delay's effect on stability is model dependent; these results do not imply monotonic stabilization by increasing RUT retention.

sources.title: Markovian embedding of fractional superdiffusion
sources.authors: P. Siegle; I. Goychuk; P. Hänggi
sources.established_overlap: Finite sums of exponential kernels and auxiliary variables represent non-Markovian dynamics.
sources.limit_of_comparison: An established representation method, not the same spatial force model or a gravitational measurement.

sources.title: Nonlinear generalized Langevin equations
sources.established_overlap: Explicit system-bath constructions generate memory and dissipation through elimination of bath variables.
sources.limit_of_comparison: No exact mapping to RUT's reciprocal Gaussian field has been established; the physical bath and any fluctuation-dissipation conditions remain separate obligations.

sources.title: Discretisation of an Oldroyd-B viscoelastic fluid flow using a Lie derivative formulation
sources.publication_status: preprint version inspected; journal status not checked
sources.established_overlap: Memory-bearing stress uses a convected derivative containing transport and deformation along fluid trajectories.
sources.limit_of_comparison: A scalar fixed-location relaxation and a transported tensor are different constitutive models; this is not gravitational evidence.

sources.title: Nonlocal Gravity Simulates Dark Matter
sources.established_overlap: Nonlocal gravitational constitutive response can mimic an extra gravitational source.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Teleparallel/nonlocal gravitational framework is not identified with the Gaussian orbital-footprint law.

sources.title: Observational tests of nonlocal gravity: Galaxy rotation curves and clusters of galaxies
sources.established_overlap: Nonlocal gravitational memory has already been applied to galaxy rotation curves and clusters.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Broad gravitational-history motivation is prior art; exact kernels, parameter meanings and dynamics differ.

sources.title: MOND--particularly as modified inertia
sources.established_overlap: Trajectory-dependent modified inertia is an established branch of nonlocal gravitational phenomenology.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Changing inertia is not the same as writing a shared scalar force field; equality of circular curves is insufficient.

sources.title: Nonlocal Gravity: Damping of Linearized Gravitational Waves
sources.established_overlap: Gravitational memory and dissipative wave propagation occur together in a nonlocal-gravity framework.
sources.limit_of_comparison: This is not RUT's source-built track, and its wave channel must not be equated to RUT retention time.

sources.title: Nonlinear nature of gravitation and gravitational-wave experiments
sources.established_overlap: Nonlinear gravitational-wave memory is a previously established use of gravitational memory.
sources.limit_of_comparison: A lasting wave-induced relative displacement is not a repeatedly reinforced attractive orbital track.

sources.title: Axiomatic approach to electromagnetic and gravitational radiation reaction of particles in curved spacetime
sources.authors: Theodore C. Quinn; Robert M. Wald
sources.established_overlap: Radiation reaction and history-sensitive self-force have a gravitational precedent.
sources.limit_of_comparison: A perturbative small-body self-force is not a universal extra galactic force or the RUT source law.

sources.title: The gravitational-wave memory effect
sources.established_overlap: Orientation reference already cited in the original rut proposal; distinguishes wave memory from ordinary oscillatory wave signals.
sources.limit_of_comparison: A review pointer, not the primary priority attribution and not evidence of an orbital-rut mechanism.

sources.title: Revisiting the gravitomagnetic clock effect
sources.locator: Version v5, 2023-12-14; journal publication 2024; original preprint 2014
sources.established_overlap: Rotation-dependent gravitational orbital effects provide context for the original vector-memory suggestion.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Ordinary frame dragging is not a rule that deepens a track every revolution; no contested coefficient is adopted here.

sources.title: Simulation of the evolution of stellar systems
sources.established_overlap: Cold balanced stellar disks can be unstable; velocity dispersion suppresses short scales while long-wavelength bar-like modes may persist.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Ordinary Newtonian disk simulations are a control, not proof that the RUT modes are the same branches or that all warm populations are stable.

sources.title: Predicting the linear response of self-gravitating stellar spheres and discs with LinearResponse.jl
sources.authors: Michael S. Petersen; Mathieu Roule; Jean-Baptiste Fouvry; Christophe Pichon; Kerwann Tep
sources.established_overlap: Action-angle/response calculations for stellar distribution functions and complex mode searches are established tools.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Adapting the interaction matrix to a Gaussian kernel and a frequency-dependent field requires verification; the warm-response method is not itself novel.

sources.title: An integral method for solving nonlinear eigenvalue problems
sources.established_overlap: Contour-integral eigensolver for nonlinear holomorphic eigenvalue problems.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Correct implementation and application are research infrastructure, not a new gravity principle. The related DOI on the arXiv page is not used as the journal DOI.

sources.title: Solving Nonlinear Eigenvalue Problems via Contour Integration and Region Partitioning
sources.established_overlap: Combines Beyn-style contour integration and recursive region partitioning to handle difficult spectra.
sources.limit_of_comparison: A current numerical comparator worth evaluating, not an automatic certification of the project's roots.

sources.title: Digital Library of Mathematical Functions: integral representations and addition theorems
sources.authors: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
sources.established_overlap: The Gaussian ring integral is an application of the established I0 angular integral; ordinary Bessel addition identities underlie wave-ring averages.
sources.limit_of_comparison: Application to a chosen physical footprint does not make the mathematical identity original.
